findings.title: The floors gate checks for a comment string, not a measured truth, and was never updated for the EMPHASIS BUDGET numbers
findings.principle: Any Stop/PreToolUse gate that claims to enforce a FLOORS LAW item must either (a) programmatically measure the rendered page against the literal in question, or (b) be documented in-repo as a ritual-only check that a downstream verifier-agent pass is mandatory before ship. A gate whose regex only checks for the presence of N characters after the word 'floors:' is not evidence the five-question pass holds, and it currently provides zero coverage of the EMPHASIS BUDGET table (weight-share <=30%, anchor ratio >=1.8x, imagery >=33%, elevation steps >=2) added four days after the gate was written. Every new floor added to LOCKFILE must, in the same commit, either extend an existing gate's checked literal or be named explicitly as verifier-only.
findings.why: A gate that can be satisfied by writing 'floors: yes all good, checked checked checked checked' creates false confidence that ceilings-without-floors problem (the exact failure UNFINISHED_AUDIT diagnosed) has been fixed at the enforcement layer, when in fact it has only been fixed at the documentation layer. This reproduces the root mechanism the audit itself named: a rule that exists on paper but isn't mechanically checked gets silently skipped under task focus, which is precisely how the 2026-07-25 flatness regression (86% weight-600, 4.7% imagery on home) shipped AFTER the FLOORS LAW was already 'owner-approved' and 'wired'.
findings.local_evidence: ~/.claude/hooks/mockup-floors-gate.py lines 19-20: `FLOORS = re.compile(r"floors:\s*\S.{20,}", re.IGNORECASE)`. The full check at line ~73 is `if FLOORS.search(text): sys.exit(0)` -- pass, no other condition. No reference anywhere in the file to weight share, anchor ratio, imagery percentage, or elevation-step count; the docstring itself only cites LOCKFILE section 17.5 (the original five-question pass, 2026-07-21) and was not touched when the EMPHASIS BUDGET table was added to LOCKFILE on 2026-07-25 (confirmed no second commit to this hook file after that date via its content, which still only mentions the five-question pass).
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn 'weight.share\|anchor.ratio\|elevation.step\|imagery.*33' ~/.claude/hooks/mockup-floors-gate.py = 0 hits. grep -rn 'EMPHASIS BUDGET' ~/.claude/hooks = 0 hits (the phrase exists only in LOCKFILE.md and CLAUDE.md, never in a hook). grep -rn 'floors:' _design-system/LOCKFILE.md CLAUDE.md _design-system/SENIOR_SCORECARD.md shows the note requirement attached only to the five-question pass, never to the later budget numbers.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: LOCKFILE section 17.5 and the mockup-floors-gate cover the ORIGINAL five-question finished-screen pass as a text-presence check. The delta this finding names: (a) even that check is text-presence, not a render-time measurement, and (b) the EMPHASIS BUDGET table (LOCKFILE, added 2026-07-25) has no gate coverage of any kind, not even text-presence.
findings.where_it_should_live: ~/.claude/hooks/mockup-floors-gate.py (extend the regex/checklist to require the emphasis-budget literals in the note, or add a companion gate) plus a one-line rule in _design-system/LOCKFILE.md EMPHASIS BUDGET section stating which gate enforces it
findings.enforcement: gate:mockup-floors-gate (extend existing) plus a mandatory verifier-agent DOM-measurement pass, matching how SENIOR_SCORECARD already splits countable-vs-judgment dimensions

findings.title: SENIOR_SCORECARD.md, the actual named ship-gate, has never been updated to include the FLOORS LAW
findings.principle: SENIOR_SCORECARD.md's five graded dimensions (Copy, Emphasis, Color, Type, Structure) must include a sixth dimension, Floors, scoring the FLOORS LAW items (imagery presence, density, edge-visibility/warmth, display anchor, emphasis-budget numbers) Pass/Half/Fail exactly like the other five. A customer-facing screen ships only at 6/6, not 5/5, from the date the FLOORS LAW existed onward.
findings.why: CLAUDE.md declares the FLOORS LAW 'CO-EQUAL with the 10 taste rules' and WORK_TYPES.md hooks SENIOR_SCORECARD in as the Axis-2 aesthetic quality gate that customer screens must pass. If the document that is actually consulted at ship time (SENIOR_SCORECARD) never grew a floors dimension, a screen can legitimately score 5/5 on the scorecard used in practice while still failing imagery/density/warmth, which is exactly the 'compliant but unfinished' failure the FLOORS LAW was written to close. A law that lives in CLAUDE.md/LOCKFILE but is absent from the one doc titled 'the ship-gate' is a law with no seat at the table where shipping decisions are actually made.
findings.local_evidence: SENIOR_SCORECARD.md, full 57-line file read: the table (lines 13-19) lists exactly 5 rows (Copy/Emphasis/Color/Type/Structure); no row for Imagery, Density, or Floors. findings.title: No ceiling or display strategy exists for when list data is genuinely RICH (a salon with 80 services, 300 reviews, a 40-photo gallery)
findings.principle: Any list-shaped surface bound by the density FLOOR (services, reviews, gallery, home sections) must also state its RICH-DATA behavior once real data exceeds roughly 3x the floor number: group by a stable dimension (service duration/category tier for services, most-recent-plus-distribution for reviews, a lightbox grid for photos beyond the first 12), or paginate/virtualize, never render the full set inline uncapped. State the exact threshold and the exact collapse mechanism per surface type in the same table that carries the density floor.
findings.why: The FLOORS LAW fixed the emptiness failure (ceilings without floors made the compliance-optimal screen the sparsest one) but did nothing about the opposite failure once real salons and content scale past seed-sized examples: a screen that renders every one of 300 reviews or 80 services inline is exactly as much a wireframe-signal as an empty one, just via a different mechanism (a wall of undifferentiated content instead of a void), and it is the more likely failure mode post-launch as real salons with mature service menus onboard, since every mockup and floor number in this system was calibrated against seed data sized at or near the floor.
findings.local_evidence: COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md SalonReviews row: 'Alle ansehen expander... Don't: review pages that need pagination, this is in-place expand' -- for a salon with 300 reviews this renders all 300 inline once expanded, no cap. COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md Select row: 'custom dropdown (typeahead/multi/virtualized) deferred to v2... don't fork a partial one' -- confirms no virtualized list primitive exists anywhere in the registry as of this pass. The density floor itself (LOCKFILE section 17, CLAUDE.md FLOORS LAW item 3) states only MINIMUMS ('services >= 6 rows', 'reviews >= 3 visible') and never a maximum or a collapse rule.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn -i 'virtualiz\|pagination\|load more\|dense list\|too many\|scales to hundreds' _design-system CLAUDE.md _rules = only hits in MOTION.md (a general aside about visual overworking, not about list length), SOURCE.md line 829 (a scroll-snap CSS aside), and the discovery feed's keyset-pagination fix (which is about scroll-repeat correctness, not display strategy for abundance). Nothing states a per-surface RICH threshold or collapse mechanism.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the density FLOOR (LOCKFILE section 17.3 / CLAUDE.md FLOORS LAW item 3) states minimums for the same surfaces (services >= 6, reviews >= 3, gallery >= 5) but is silent on maximums or collapse behavior above roughly 3x those numbers.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md section 17.3 (density floor), add a paired richness ceiling row per surface; components/SalonReviews.md and the Select registry row for the virtualization deferral
findings.enforcement: checklist (design-verifier check on a real, non-seed salon fixture with 50+ services once one exists) plus a component-level TODO tracked in COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md

findings.title: No defined state for SPARSE-BUT-REAL content: the FLOORS LAW binds unconditionally in production even for a legitimately thin new salon
findings.principle: A production customer screen showing real (non-null, non-fabricated) but genuinely thin content -- a newly onboarded salon with 2 photos and 0 reviews, below every density-floor number -- is not the same case as EmptyState (zero data) and is not exempt from the FLOORS LAW by any of the named exemptions (forms, checkout, legal, receipts). State explicitly which floors still bind (no-fabrication, category-icon fallback) and which are waived (the >=5 gallery / >=3 reviews counts) for a salon below the density floor on real data, so a new vendor's page does not either fail an unstateable gate or silently get exempted with no rule saying so.
findings.why: FLOORS LAW section 17.3 already states the boundary problem exists for MOCKUPS ('a target-state mockup renders full seeded content plus a one-line footer naming what is not yet wired') but that boundary line was written for design artifacts, not for what a real production page renders once a genuinely small salon signs up. Pre-launch, most onboarding salons will be exactly this case (thin real data, not fabricated, not seed-sized), and the density and imagery floors as written give no guidance for it, which risks either (a) engineers quietly special-casing thin salons with no written rule, reintroducing the silent-inconsistency problem this whole law system exists to prevent, or (b) a thin-but-real salon page reading as broken because it cannot hit floor numbers with honest data.
findings.local_evidence: LOCKFILE section 17.1 imagery floor and CLAUDE.md density-floor contract row list exemptions BY NAME as 'forms, checkout payment, legal, receipts' only -- a real salon PDP with insufficient photography or fewer than 5 gallery images is not on that list, so the floor technically still binds it with no stated fallback beyond the generic missing-photo icon treatment, which was designed for a single missing photo, not for an entire salon that legitimately has 2.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i 'thin salon\|new vendor\|below.*floor\|sparse.*real\|onboarding.*density\|legitimately.*sparse' _design-system CLAUDE.md = 0 hits. The only boundary language found is LOCKFILE section 17 flaw-3 text about MOCKUPS ('a target-state mockup... one-line footer naming what is not yet wired'), which is explicitly scoped to design artifacts, confirmed by re-reading the sentence in context.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: SOURCE.md section 10 empty-state machinery covers the ZERO-data case; LOCKFILE section 17 boundary language covers the MOCKUP case. Neither covers PRODUCTION content that is real, non-zero, and below the density floor.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/SOURCE.md section 10 (add a 'below-floor real content' state alongside empty/loading/error) and CLAUDE.md's density-floor contract row
findings.enforcement: checklist plus a design-verifier check run against a seeded thin-salon fixture (2 photos, 0 reviews, 3 services) rather than only the ideal-density fixture

findings.title: No trust floor: the finished-screen pass does not require cancellation terms, provider identity, or a price breakdown before a commit action
findings.principle: Every screen carrying a paid commit action (a Bezahlen/pay button, a booking confirmation) must pass a trust floor in addition to the five-question finished-screen pass: (1) the total price is broken down (base + surcharge + VAT if applicable), (2) the cancellation/refund term is visible in the DOM, not merely defined in a labels object, before the commit button, and (3) who the user is booking with (stylist/salon name, not just a category) is visible above the commit action. All three are Pass/Fail gates alongside the existing five.
findings.why: A booking or payment screen that hits every hierarchy/density floor (a photo, a big number, a semantic color, no dead-grey) can still leave the customer committing money without knowing they can get it back, which is a business-risk gap the FLOORS LAW's aesthetic framing does not touch. WCAG and design-maturity concerns aside, this is a first-principles commerce requirement: Swiss consumer-protection norms and basic marketplace trust both require the cancellation term be visible at the point of commitment, not merely present somewhere in the copy dictionary. Pre-launch framing: this is a gap that would erode trust and likely drive support tickets once real customers pay real money, not a live incident today.
findings.local_evidence: app/[locale]/walk-in-pay/page.tsx defines cancelPolicy in all four locale label objects (line 308-311, e.g. de: 'Kostenlose Stornierung bis zum Aufruf') but grep confirms it is referenced 4 times total in the file, all 4 being the definitions themselves inside the labels object -- zero JSX render sites (`grep -c 't.cancelPolicy}'` returns 0). This is the exact defect research/PSYCH_AUDIT_2026-07-07.md already found and flagged as a lever ('a customer sees a bare CHF 45 bezahlen button with no stated cancellation policy before committing their card'); it remains unfixed as of 2026-07-26, roughly three weeks later, and no FLOORS-LAW-tier rule would have caught it because no version of the finished-screen pass checks for it.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i 'trust floor\|cancellation.*floor\|price.*breakdown.*floor\|refund.*visible' _design-system/LOCKFILE.md CLAUDE.md _design-system/SENIOR_SCORECARD.md _design-system/RESTRAINT_TEST.md = 0 hits. LOCKFILE section 17.5's five-question pass covers only photographic focal / one-biggest-element / tabular number / semantic color / dead-grey -- none of the five is a commerce-trust check.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: PSYCHOLOGY.md's price-transparency law (a different domain file) covers the underlying psychology principle in the abstract, and PSYCH_AUDIT_2026-07-07.md already named this exact instance as a lever three weeks ago, but neither has been converted into a FLOORS-LAW-tier gate, and the underlying bug is still live in the code, which is the delta this finding names.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md section 17.5 (add a trust-floor row alongside the five-question pass) and CLAUDE.md FLOORS LAW block item 1
findings.enforcement: gate: a small static check that any file rendering a Stripe/pay confirm button also renders a cancellation-policy string in the same component (catches exactly the walk-in-pay case), plus a verifier-agent checklist item

findings.title: No dense-screen mirror of the trapped-dead-space rule: nothing bounds how far a user must scroll past content to reach the primary commit action
findings.principle: On any screen with a single primary commit action (Buchen, Bezahlen, Weiter), the action must be reachable via a sticky/fixed control OR must appear within roughly one additional viewport height of scroll from the point all required inputs are satisfied, regardless of how much content (services, reviews, gallery) precedes it on the page. State the maximum scroll distance the way NEVER-AGAIN floor 3 states the maximum dead-space percentage.
findings.why: NEVER-AGAIN floor 3 already recognizes and fixes the SPARSE failure of this exact shape ('trapped dead space below the primary action must be < 30% of the viewport') for empty states, but the identical failure in the opposite direction, a primary action buried below an unbounded amount of dense content once the density floor is satisfied or exceeded, has no matching rule. A screen that correctly hits every density-floor minimum (services >= 6, reviews >= 3) but stacks them all above the commit button without a sticky bar has traded one navigation problem (an empty screen with a stranded CTA) for another (a full screen with a buried CTA), and only the first direction is currently a named floor.
findings.local_evidence: CLAUDE.md NEVER-AGAIN floor 3 states the dead-space ceiling only for EmptyState-shaped screens ('trapped dead space below the primary action must be < 30% of the viewport... The payment empty state shipped with the CTA at 54% down and 46% dead space'). RESTRAINT_TEST.md's fix-direction list for booking flow separately recommends 'a running summary sticky bottom bar from step 1' as a suggestion, not as a locked numeric floor, and SOURCE.md line 1295 documents a sticky-CTA component exists for booking specifically, but there is no general rule requiring it, or bounding scroll distance, on every commit-bearing screen (e.g. a long service-selection list with no sticky total).
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i 'scroll.*before\|reachable within\|max scroll\|one screen away\|buried.*cta\|cta.*below.*fold' _design-system CLAUDE.md = 0 hits beyond the thumb-reach zone research (RATIONALE.md, PSYCH_PSYCHOLOGY.md), which argues for bottom placement generally but states no scroll-distance ceiling tied to content density.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the sparse-side rule exists by name (NEVER-AGAIN floor 3) and a sticky-CTA component exists for the booking flow specifically (SOURCE.md line 1295); the delta is that no rule generalizes the sticky-CTA requirement to every commit-bearing screen, and no numeric ceiling exists for the dense-side failure the way one exists for the sparse-side failure.
findings.where_it_should_live: CLAUDE.md NEVER-AGAIN design floors block (add floor 3b, the dense-screen mirror of floor 3) and _design-system/LOCKFILE.md's sticky-CTA / design-contract row
findings.enforcement: checklist (design-verifier measures scroll distance to CTA on the rendered page) -- not easily a static gate since it depends on content volume at render time

findings.title: Colour has a presence floor and a sparseness ceiling, but no measured budget pair the way type weight does
findings.principle: State the colour-emphasis budget with the same measured-range structure as the EMPHASIS BUDGET weight-share table: name the maximum share of first-viewport pixels that may carry non-neutral chroma (distinct from the existing blue-sparseness rule, which governs WHERE blue goes, not how much total colour a screen carries) and reconcile it explicitly against the 'at least one semantic-color moment' presence floor, labelling the number CONV since no external source exists for a chroma-count threshold (same honesty standard TASTE_RANGE.md already applied to the weight-share and ratio numbers).
findings.why: The system already got this exact category of number wrong once: TASTE_RANGE.md found the EMPHASIS BUDGET's weight-share, ratio, imagery-share, and elevation-step literals all had no external source and needed to be explicitly relabelled CONV rather than presented as research-derived. Colour is the one channel in the same budget table that has a presence rule (finished-screen pass item 4) and a sparseness rule (taste rule 3, blue is sparse) but no measured RANGE the way weight and size now do, which is the exact gap-shape (a ceiling and a floor exist in prose but were never joined into one measured table) that produced the flatness regression for weight and size in the first place.
findings.local_evidence: TASTE_RANGE.md NOT-SUPPORTED item 7, verbatim: 'No evidence that a COUNT of chromatic colours is a floor. FLATNESS_DIAGNOSIS counted 2 on home and 3 on PDP and read it as a symptom... no source states a minimum number of hues a screen needs. If a chroma floor is wanted, it has to be argued from FLOORS LAW 1's at least one semantic-color moment, which is a presence rule, not a count.' This is the research itself naming the exact absence and explicitly declining to fill it, leaving the gap open rather than resolved.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i 'chroma\|colour.*budget\|color.*budget\|colour.*share\|hue.*count' _design-system/LOCKFILE.md _design-system/research/TASTE_RANGE.md CLAUDE.md shows the concept discussed only in TASTE_RANGE.md's NOT-SUPPORTED section, and it is explicitly left unresolved there, not adopted anywhere else in LOCKFILE or CLAUDE.md.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: taste rule 3 (blue is sparse, WHERE not HOW MUCH) and FLOORS LAW item 4/finished-screen-pass item 4 (a semantic-color moment must be present) both touch colour, but neither states a measured range the way the weight-share/ratio table now does for type, and TASTE_RANGE.md names this gap by name without closing it.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md EMPHASIS BUDGET table (add a colour row, explicitly labelled CONV per the evidence-tier convention already used for the other five rows)

findings.title: Worst-case content (longest name, longest review, most services) is an optional verifier step, not a FLOORS-LAW gate item, even though several floors can visibly break under it
findings.principle: Every mockup and every customer-screen ship check must render against a named worst-case content fixture (longest real or plausible salon name, a full-length review, a maximally long service name) as a hard, non-optional line item inside the finished-screen pass, not as an 'only when in scope' edge case in the generic verifier loop. Name the specific floors it stress-tests: the two-ink-anchor card rule (a long name plus a price can no longer both fit at their locked sizes), the >=28px display-anchor rule (a long headline at 28px+ may wrap awkwardly), and the no-truncation-of-load-bearing-copy rule.
findings.why: The generic verifier-loop protocol (global CLAUDE.md rule 9) already lists 'long content' as something to check, but qualifies it 'only when in scope', which under task focus means it is the first thing skipped, exactly the mechanism the FLOORS LAW itself diagnosed for density and imagery ('subtraction can never trip a gate'). None of the FLOORS-LAW-specific mechanisms (the five-question pass, the EMPHASIS BUDGET table, the mockup-floors-gate) mention worst-case content at all, so a mockup can be built, gated, and shipped using only comfortably-sized seed strings and never discover that its two-anchor card rule or 28px display floor breaks the moment a real Zurich salon with a 40-character name is seeded in.
findings.local_evidence: Global CLAUDE.md rule 9 ('What to verify in EACH round') lists 'Edge cases: empty data, long content, error states (only when in scope)' as the fourth of four bullets, explicitly optional. LOCKFILE section 17.5's five-question pass and the EMPHASIS BUDGET table (both read in full) contain no reference to content length, truncation, or a worst-case fixture at all.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i 'longest\|worst.case\|stress.test\|long name\|long content' _design-system/LOCKFILE.md _design-system/CLAUDE.md _design-system/SENIOR_SCORECARD.md _design-system/RESTRAINT_TEST.md returns 0 hits inside any FLOORS-LAW-specific document; the only hit for 'long content' anywhere in the estate is the generic, optional verifier-loop bullet in the global CLAUDE.md, which is a different, non-FLOORS-tied mechanism.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the generic verifier-loop rule 9 in global CLAUDE.md already names long-content as a thing to check, but marks it optional and does not tie it to any specific FLOORS LAW literal (two-anchor rule, 28px display floor) the way this finding does.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md section 17.5 (add worst-case-content as item 6 of the finished-screen pass) and _design-system/SENIOR_SCORECARD.md dimension 5 (Structure) or the new Floors dimension proposed in hierarchy-density-02
findings.enforcement: checklist (design-verifier renders the mockup with a seeded worst-case string set, not just the ideal-density set)

findings.title: The imagery and density floors were never reconciled with the existing LCP <= 2.5s performance gate
findings.principle: Wherever the imagery floor (>=33% of the first viewport, PDP gallery >=5 photos) or the density floor is stated, name which image in that set is priority-loaded (next/image priority prop, no lazy) to protect Largest Contentful Paint, and which are deferred. State this once, in the same table that carries the imagery floor, rather than leaving it to be independently re-derived per surface.
findings.why: The FLOORS LAW's entire mechanism for fixing the 'beta' perception is to mandate more, larger, earlier photography on exactly the surfaces (home, PDP, browse) the per-wave ship gate already holds to LCP <=2.5s. Two correct rules pulling in opposite directions with no reconciliation is a latent regression: a team that satisfies the imagery floor by adding a large above-the-fold photo without marking it priority can quietly blow the LCP gate, and a team protecting LCP by lazy-loading everything can quietly fail the imagery floor, and neither failure is visible to the other rule's own gate.
findings.local_evidence: LOCKFILE.md line 990/1028 states the per-wave verifier gate requires 'LCP <=2.5s' as a hard number. LOCKFILE section 17.1 (added 2026-07-21) and the EMPHASIS BUDGET imagery row (added 2026-07-25) both mandate the largest element of every SalonCard be a photo and >=33% first-viewport imagery share, with no cross-reference to the LCP gate or to next/image's priority mechanism (SOURCE.md line 830 only notes lazy-loading is 'already default for next/image, worth confirming', which is the opposite direction from what the imagery floor needs on the hero image specifically).
findings.absence_proof: grep -n -i 'priority=\|next/image.*priority\|LCP.*imagery\|imagery.*LCP' _design-system/LOCKFILE.md _design-system/SOURCE.md CLAUDE.md returns 0 hits connecting the two concepts; each exists in its own section of LOCKFILE with no forward or backward reference.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: both the LCP gate and the imagery floor independently exist and are each individually well-specified; the delta is the absence of any rule connecting them, which is a cross-cutting gap rather than a missing concept.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md section 17.1 (imagery floor, add one sentence naming the priority-load requirement) with a cross-reference to the per-wave LCP gate in WORK_TYPES.md
findings.enforcement: checklist (Lighthouse LCP check already exists per-wave; add a one-line code-review note that the hero/gallery-first image must carry the priority prop)
